numerical_failure.observed_behavior: scipy.stats.yeojohnson_llf loses precision for tightly clustered data and overflows for extreme lambda values because the log-likelihood was computed via the constant term and a direct log of the variance; the issue is reported as precision loss and overflow in the Yeo-Johnson log-likelihood
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: yeojohnson_llf should return accurate log-likelihood values without precision loss or overflow, computing the log-variance term in the log domain and dropping the constant term
trigger_conditions: lmb in the extreme range such as -14, -20, or 16, 20 with negated data
all-positive or all-negative data path where abs(lmb) or abs(lmb - 2) is very small (numerical instability)
oracle_clues: PR#24172 plots llf versus lmb before and after the fix, and compares yeojohnson_llf(lmb, data) with yeojohnson_llf(-lmb, -data) symmetry
Empty-array case returns NaN via _get_nan in the fixed code

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: all-negative or all-positive data (e.g., data [10, 10, 10, 9.9] with lmb values -14, 16, -20, 20); precision loss arises when the constant term is retained, overflow arises at the larger |lmb| values
category_specific_evidence: Test test_gh24172 uses data = xp.asarray([10, 10, 10, 9.9], dtype=xp.float64) and checks yeojohnson_llf results with rtol=1e-7 against expected values computed with mpsci at mpmath.mp.dps=100.

Expected values in the test: lmb=-14 and lmb=16 (with -data) both give 12.418595783381280 (precision loss case); lmb=-20 gives 12.360966379200528 and lmb=20 (with -data) gives 12.380287243698629 (overflow case).

The PR and discussion state that removing the constant term avoids precision loss only when data is all negative or all positive; the constant cannot be removed for mixed-sign data, and the fix special-cases all-pos/neg data.

The code computes dtype via xp_result_type(lmb, data, force_floating=True) and uses eps = xp.finfo(dtype).eps; it special-cases abs(lmb) < eps and numerical instability when abs(lmb) or abs(lmb - 2) is very small.
The reproduction example in the discussion calls yeojohnson_llf(-14, data) and yeojohnson_llf(16, -data) on data = np.array([10, 10, 10, 9.9]), described as no overflow, just precision loss.
The log-variance is computed in log-domain to avoid overflow; the old code used xp.var followed by xp.log with a smallest_normal guard.
reproduction_risks: Mixed-sign data is explicitly left unchanged (constant term retained), so reproductions using mixed data will not exercise the fixed path.
JAX JIT behavior was unresolved in the discussion ('If it doesn't work with JAX JIT...'), and an empty-array case in JAX was mentioned in the commit.
The discussion notes further pathological case when sigma^2 is very small and data is tightly clustered at zero, which was not resolved.
Expected values are only given to 17 significant digits with rtol=1e-7; a reproduction must match the mpmath-computed references rather than the old implementation output.
